title: Design UPI (Unified Payments Interface)
subtitle: VPA resolution, switch-coordinated interbank debit/credit, and deferred net settlement

stages.title: Stage 1 — Naive Direct Bank-to-Bank Transfer
stages.bottleneck: Every bank must integrate directly with every other bank (O(N²) connections at national scale), and paying by raw account number + IFSC is error-prone — a typo sends money to the wrong person irreversibly.
stages.narrative: **Direct Bank-to-Bank.** Paying anyone means knowing their exact account number and IFSC code, and every bank pair needs its own direct integration to move money — this doesn't scale past a handful of banks, and a mistyped account number is unrecoverable.

stages.title: Stage 2 — NPCI Switch, VPA Resolution & Two-Phase Debit/Credit
stages.bottleneck: Debit and credit now happen in two completely independent banks' ledgers — there's no shared database transaction spanning both, so a naive implementation risks debiting the payer and never crediting the payee if the second leg fails.
stages.narrative:
**Switch-Coordinated Transfer.**
1. **VPA Resolution:** the switch resolves `ravi@okhdfc` to a real account *before* any money moves, catching typos early.
2. **Debit-first, confirm-then-credit:** the switch debits the remitter bank, and only on success asks the beneficiary bank to credit. If the credit leg fails, the switch issues a compensating reversal back to the remitter bank — keyed by the same `txn_ref` so a retried reversal is never double-applied.
3. Every bank integrates once with the switch instead of with every other bank (O(N) instead of O(N²)).

stages.title: Stage 3 — Deferred Net Settlement & Mandates
stages.bottleneck: Settling every single transaction as its own interbank wire would flood the settlement rail with millions of tiny transfers a day, and unchecked recurring mandates could let a merchant debit far more than the user actually authorized.

edges.label: Check active mandate before scheduled debit
Aggregate net obligation per bank pair
Periodic net settlement + reconcile against bank ledgers

stages.narrative: **Deferred Net Settlement & Mandates.** Users get instant, final-feeling confirmation on every transaction, but the actual money movement between banks is batched: the switch nets out what each bank pair owes each other and settles only the difference periodically, instead of one real wire transfer per transaction. Recurring payments (mandates) pre-authorize future debits up to a capped amount and validity window, checked by the switch before each scheduled execution — the user's PIN authorizes the mandate once, not every cycle.
